extracted.intended_audience: educated readers, policymakers and reformers interested in electoral/constitutional design; and experimental physicists interested in radiant-heat experiments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for designing and judging elective government institutions (franchise, representation, assemblies, constitutional amendment), together with methodological standards for experimental work on radiant heat (controls, replication, elimination of artifacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local institutions on the elective principle as basis
rubrics_metrics.description: A wise arrangement of local institutions on the elective principle would of course be the basis of the system, as it is the indispensable training-school of the people in self-government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local elective institutions train citizens in self-government and should form the foundation for higher representative structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elections to the central Legislature by installments
rubrics_metrics.description: The elections to the central Legislature ... ought to be by installments, a mode which would allow the steady inflow of public opinion, and at the same time prevent cataclysms such as now attend general elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staggered/installed elections reduce disruptive mass swings caused by special agitations and maintain steady public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed terms and end of ministerial prerogative of dissolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The term for which each member of the central Legislature was elected would be fixed, and there would be an end of the ministerial prerogative of dissolution, which has run into grave abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixing terms and removing executive power to dissolve the legislature prevents opportunistic dissolutions used to perpetuate ministerial power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect election of central Legislature by local Legislatures
rubrics_metrics.description: The election of a central Legislature by local Legislatures ... would no doubt be a tame affair compared with the turmoil of a general election under the present system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting central representatives via local assemblies can reduce national-level demagoguery and turmoil, providing more responsible selection under community oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribunal for political corruption and criminalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Political corruption ... should be distinctly stamped as a crime, and brought under the regular cognizance of justice. For this purpose ... a tribunal is needed free from partisan influence and open for the reception of charges brought against men in public trusts by any citizen, with proper safeguards against wantonness or malice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create an independent, non-partisan tribunal to adjudicate political offenses, allowing citizen-initiated charges with safeguards to prevent abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of minorities tends to torpid compromise
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation of minorities seems to have done but little good. The result is a torpid compromise ... the minority member is nailed to his seat, and can neither take office nor retire, except at a general election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex schemes for minority representation can entrench minority holders and discourage responsive contests; beware of arrangements that make members immovable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a second ballot (runoff) when no absolute majority
rubrics_metrics.description: The only measure of this kind which appears to promise real improvement is the adoption of the second ballot when no candidate has polled an absolute majority at the first. This would give opinion ... a fairer chance against a compact interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement runoffs to enable independent candidates and split opinions to coalesce against entrenched interests; counters the 'wasted vote' argument used by wire-pullers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit assembly size for effective deliberation
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience seems distinctly to have shown that, to make an assembly deliberative, its numbers must be limited. In a Parliament of six hundred or a thousand members ... deliberation is impossible. More than two hundred can hardly take counsel together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep representative bodies reasonably small (ideally ≤ ~200) to enable genuine deliberation; if larger, structure committees so deliberative work is effective and not constantly re-opened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grand committees only effective if dominant party majorities arranged
rubrics_metrics.description: There is the resource of grand committees, which, however, is not available with party government, unless the committees are so arranged that the dominant party shall have a majority in each of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using committees to manage large assemblies, ensure practical composition so committees can make decisions without constant reversal by the full house under party government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine indirect election with widely extended suffrage
rubrics_metrics.description: With such a mode of election to the central Legislature as has been suggested, it will be safe to combine a widely extended suffrage. It will be safe, and it will be politic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect selection to the central body permits broader enfranchisement of the populace without the same risks present under direct mass elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger of universal suffrage arises when paired with party government and direct elections
rubrics_metrics.description: The danger arises not from universal suffrage by itself, but from universal suffrage in conjunction with party government and direct elections. It is as the tool of faction and its demagogues that the rowdy is politically formidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess suffrage reforms in context: coupling mass franchise with strong party-directed direct elections can empower demagogues and factional manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education qualification preferable to property qualification for voters
rubrics_metrics.description: Property qualifications are odious ... On the other hand, an education qualification is not odious; the writer ... has always found that artisan audiences receive the mention of it with favor; it is most reasonable, since a man can hardly give an intelligent vote ... by voting without the common organs of intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer literacy/education tests (e.g., ability to read; school certificate under full education) over property tests to ensure informed voting, while being sensitive to excluding disadvantaged workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid requiring writing for voter registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing, perhaps, ought hardly to be required, for the horny hand of the farm-laborer may lose that faculty without default of brain or heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make voter qualifications practicable—reading may be required, but writing should be eschewed as it unfairly penalizes manual workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: All voters liable to civic duties (defense, jury service)
rubrics_metrics.description: All voters ought also to be liable to every civic duty, such as that of national defense, and that of serving on juries, if the system of jury-trial is retained on its present footing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie franchise to civic obligations to balance rights and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer self-disfranchisement to disfranchisement by exclusive legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sifting process is necessary, let it be one of self-disfranchisement by refusal of equitable conditions, rather than one of disfranchisement by exclusive legislation; the popular feeling that government rests on the broad basis of equality and justice will be less impaired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow voluntary opt-out based on equitable conditions rather than legally imposed exclusions, to preserve legitimacy of equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study the sentiment of republics and allow abstention to sift electorate
rubrics_metrics.description: The sentiment of monarchies and aristocracies has been studied; it is now time to study the sentiment of republics. A good deal of sifting ... would probably be done by abstention, when there were no longer organized factions to marshal the irresponsible, and march them to the poll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize abstention as a democratic sifting mechanism in a mature republic where factional mobilization is absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal suffrage should be proportioned to financial contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief, almost the only function of a city government in these days, is to raise and expend money; in equity and reason, therefore, the franchise ought to be in some measure proportioned to the amount of the contribution; it ought to follow the rule of joint-stock companies, rather than that of political communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For municipal elections, consider weighting franchise in proportion to tax/contribution, since city government primarily manages finances and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cities require strong, permanent, pure and enlightened administration of business/scientific character
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong, permanent, pure, and enlightened administration, of a thoroughly business and scientific character, is what is needed by the people of every city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Municipal governance should prioritize stable, technocratic administration focused on public health, comfort, and efficient service delivery—especially for poorer quarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider potential adverse social effects before extending female suffrage
rubrics_metrics.description: The spheres of the two sexes ... coequal but distinct ... Law ... rests at bottom upon the force of the community, and the force of the community is male. ... Would the men allow the women to vote them into a war? ... women are hereby rendered untrustworthy counselors in questions of peace and war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Author's argument) Evaluate female suffrage by considering claimed impacts on accountability, defense, family structure and the temperament of public life. Note: historically contested and polemical claims on women's political roles are presented as criteria to be weighed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware that suffrage movements can be linked to broader social changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The suffrage movement ... is ... part of a movement against the limitations of sex, against the bondage of matrimony and the burdens of maternity. Those who are thus striving to break up the political unity of the family are assailing its integrity in other ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing enfranchisement movements, consider their wider social/political objectives and potential consequences for family and social order (as argued by the author).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret ballot: removes external pressure but may shield follies and not defeat wire-pullers
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion that [the ballot] would specially favour Liberalism is at an end. It annuls all pressure ... On the other hand, it affords a cover for individual follies and for all the motives which shun the light. It has failed to baffle the wire-puller ... he always succeeds in convincing the mass of electors that a vote given for any but a regular party-candidate will be lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate secret ballot by balancing reduced coercion against hiding uninformed or capricious votes and recognizing that organizational persuasion may still defeat independent choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwritten traditions (British constitution) not suitable for new democracies
rubrics_metrics.description: The British Constitution is unwritten, and therefore elastic, ... but, like many things ... it forms no precedent for other nations. In new-born democracies nothing will prevent the militant politician from using ... all the powers which the letter of the law puts into his hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New or young democracies should avoid relying on unwritten constitutional conventions; prefer explicit, written constraints to prevent abuse by ambitious politicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Young commonwealths require a written, strict constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: A young commonwealth requires a written constitution, and a strict one. Moreover, the document ... is an instrument of no small power in educating the citizen, and has a conservative influence ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a clear written constitution to educate citizens and provide stable constraints on political actors in nascent states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional amendment power should be vested in the nation and have a practicable mode
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment of the Constitution ought to be distinctly vested in the nation at large ... and a mode should be provided by which the sovereign can exercise the power ... provide that it should be lawful at any election ... for the electors to inscribe on the same ticket a requisition for the submission of a constitutional amendment, and that the Legislature should be bound to submit the amendment to a plebiscite, if a certain proportion of the electorate had supported the requisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mechanisms by which popular will, expressed at elections, can require submission of constitutional amendments to plebiscite, ensuring the nation can reform entrenched assemblies without revolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elective assemblies will not voluntarily reform themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: An elective assembly will not terminate its own existence, or even pass a measure of reform affecting the position of a large portion of its members, if it can help doing so, any more than a king will abdicate of his own accord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design external or popular triggers to constitutional change because incumbent representative bodies are unlikely to self-reform voluntarily when it threatens their position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single central assembly elected by local assemblies and electing the executive is preferable long-term
rubrics_metrics.description: A single central assembly elected by the members of local assemblies, and itself electing the executive, will after sufficient experience be the form finally assumed by elective governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional designs where local assemblies select central representatives, and the central assembly selects the executive, as a systematic alternative to party-based direct elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat and verify experiments with diverse sources and tube conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Former experiments were repeated and verified with divers sources of heat, and with experimental tubes, some polished within, and others coated inside with lamp-black. The results obtained with the one class of tubes are substantially the same as those obtained with the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replicate experiments across multiple source types and apparatus surface conditions to ensure robustness of observed effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate internal reflection as potential artifact
rubrics_metrics.description: But even a coating of lamp-black may be supposed to reflect a certain amount of heat, hence the desirability of an arrangement whereby internal reflection should be entirely abolished. This was accomplished ... a calorific beam was sent along the axis of the experimental tube without at all impinging upon its interior surface. No reflection came into play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experimental geometry so that the beam does not interact with container surfaces, removing internal reflection as a confounding factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use well-characterized sources (e.g., platinum spiral, lime cylinder) and control temperature
rubrics_metrics.description: A spiral of platinum wire, rendered incandescent by a voltaic current of measured strength, was chosen as source of heat ... When the source of heat was changed to a carefully worked cylinder of lime ... the results were confirmatory of those obtained with the spiral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ measured, controllable heat sources and cross-check results with fundamentally different sources to rule out source-specific artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condense radiation via lenses or mirrors and compare methods
rubrics_metrics.description: To condense the radiation from the lime-light, concave mirrors were sometimes employed, and sometimes rock-salt lenses. The results in both cases were identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple optical condensation methods (mirrors, lenses) and verify that method choice does not change results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce apparatus self-radiation/absorption by polished internal silver surface
rubrics_metrics.description: The experimental tube recently employed was provided with an internal silver surface, deposited electrolytically and highly polished. By this arrangement the radiation of the tube itself, as well as its absorption, was rendered quite insensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize apparatus emission/absorption by well-chosen internal coatings (e.g., polished silver) to avoid contamination of measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimentum crucis: vary path length/distance to test vapor vs liquid-film absorption hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: If the observed absorptions be due to such liquid films, then the separation of the salts more widely from each other, the space between them being copiously supplied with vapor, ought to produce no effect; but if the absorption ... be the act of the vapor-molecules, then the deepening of the absorbing stratum ought to produce an augmented effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform decisive tests by varying the thickness/depth of the gaseous layer between windows: increasing absorption with depth supports molecular (intra-gaseous) absorption over surface-film hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative demonstration that absorption increases with gas-layer thickness
rubrics_metrics.description: With sulphuric-ether vapor, the distance between the plates being one twentieth of an inch, an absorption of two per cent was observed. ... in passing from one twentieth of an inch to two inches the absorption rose from two per cent to thirty-five per cent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report quantitative changes in absorption with experimental parameter variations to provide strong empirical evidence against alternative explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare vapors and parent liquids: order of absorption should match
rubrics_metrics.description: When vapors, in quantities proportional to the densities of their liquids, were examined ... the order of their absorptions was precisely that of the liquids from which they were derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare absorption spectra/strengths of vapors and their parent liquids; concordant ordering supports intra-molecular absorption mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disprove vapor-hesion (liquid-film) hypothesis by multiple lines of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Such experiments, recently verified, entirely dispose of the hypothesis that liquid films were the cause of the observed absorption. The vapor-hesion hypothesis involves the assumption that liquids exert on radiant heat an absorbent power which is denied to their vapors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geometry, depth-dependence, surface conditioning, and cross-source replication to rule out surface-film explanations before attributing absorption to molecular processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use previously employed apparatus and long-term verification
rubrics_metrics.description: An experimental tube of the dimensions here given was employed by the lecturer to check his results more than ten years ago. ... To obviate [old tube emission issues], the experimental tube recently employed was provided with an internal silver surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference and reuse prior apparatus/approaches to validate consistency over time, while updating to mitigate known issues.
